title: Infective Endocarditis: Recognition, Blood Cultures and Urgent Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition, microbiological sampling, imaging and endocarditis-team escalation for suspected infective endocarditis.
findings: The named primary guideline was opened and the cited sections were used.
Normal values are descriptive; use local laboratory and age/pregnancy ranges.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was identified in the opened Saudi MOH protocol index.
SFDA registration and hospital formulary availability were not verified; no drug dose is supplied.

pathophysiology.summary: Bloodstream organisms adhere to susceptible endocardial or prosthetic surfaces. Vegetation can destroy valves and cause heart failure or abscess. Emboli and immune phenomena can injure brain, spleen, kidney and other organs.
keyMechanisms: Bloodstream organisms adhere to susceptible endocardial or prosthetic surfaces.
Vegetation can destroy valves and cause heart failure or abscess.
Emboli and immune phenomena can injure brain, spleen, kidney and other organs.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

symptoms: Fever, rigors, fatigue, breathlessness, weight loss, focal pain or neurological symptoms.
physicalSigns: New or changing murmur, heart failure, embolic signs, vascular/immunological lesions or persistent bacteraemia.
redFlags: Pulmonary oedema, shock, conduction block, focal neurology, persistent sepsis, prosthetic-valve/device infection or large embolic burden.
precipitants: Prosthetic valve, previous endocarditis, cardiac device, structural heart disease, haemodialysis, injection drug use or recent bacteraemia.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: No endocardial imaging finding or persistent clinical pattern; organism and host risk still matter.
Sterile vegetation in malignancy/autoimmune disease with negative microbiology.
Systemic inflammatory features without a microbiological or endocardial source.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Apply the current ESC-modified diagnostic criteria using microbiology, imaging and clinical features; do not use one negative study to exclude high-probability disease.

ruleIn.testName: Three sets of peripheral blood cultures
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Obtain before antibiotics when the patient is stable enough; sample separate venepunctures and document timing.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

ruleIn.normalValue: No vegetation or new destructive lesion
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Vegetation, new regurgitation, abscess or prosthetic complication
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: First-line cardiac imaging; a negative test does not exclude high-risk disease.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Vegetation, abscess, prosthetic/device infection or destructive lesion
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Use when suspicion remains high, prosthetic/device infection is possible or transthoracic imaging is inadequate.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

ruleOut.normalValue: No new conduction or organ abnormality
ruleOut.expectedFinding: Conduction block, renal injury or embolic complication
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: New conduction disease can indicate peri-annular extension and requires urgent escalation.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

clinicalManagement.title: Stabilise and obtain cultures
actions: Treat shock or heart failure and obtain three blood-culture sets before antibiotics when this is safe.
If unstable, take cultures promptly and start the local empirical endocarditis regimen without avoidable delay.

clinicalManagement.title: Image valves and complications
actions: Arrange transthoracic echocardiography followed by transoesophageal imaging when indicated.
Use brain/body imaging for focal or embolic complications through the specialist pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Activate the endocarditis team
actions: Discuss with cardiology, infectious diseases/microbiology and cardiac surgery.
Escalate heart failure, uncontrolled infection, abscess/conduction block and embolic-risk features for early surgical assessment.

medicationPlan.note: Empirical and organism-directed regimens depend on native/prosthetic valve, acquisition setting, organism, renal function and local resistance; use the endocarditis-team protocol. No medicine dose may be prescribed from this draft. Use the current Saudi hospital formulary and specialty-approved protocol; verify allergy, pregnancy/age, renal and hepatic function.

teaching.scope: Recognition, microbiological sampling, imaging and endocarditis-team escalation for suspected infective endocarditis.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Pulmonary oedema, shock, conduction block, focal neurology, persistent sepsis, prosthetic-valve/device infection or large embolic burden.
Discuss with cardiology, infectious diseases/microbiology and cardiac surgery.
pitfalls: Delaying escalation while waiting for non-essential tests.
Using an unverified medicine regimen instead of the current local protocol.

references.title: 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of endocarditis

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Not suitable for routine discharge before endocarditis-team assessment; outpatient treatment requires a formal specialist plan and stability criteria.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: The endocarditis team defines antimicrobial duration, repeat cultures/imaging, surgery, oral health and relapse surveillance.
